meta.title: Keres — Organize universes, connect narratives
meta.description: An offline-first story planning platform for mobile, web, and desktop, with optional sync across devices.

hero.title: Organize universes, connect narratives, and write anywhere.
hero.lead: Keres brings characters, locations, chapters, scenes, choices, items, world rules, notes, and media into one workspace. The app keeps working without a network. A server only comes in when you want to sync, collaborate, or publish.

offline.title: Offline-first for real
offline.body: Every story lives in a local SQLite database. Plan on a train, a plane, or the sofa. When a network and a server are there, sync ships the changes and handles version conflicts.

universe.title: The universe, not the manuscript
universe.body: Keres is not a text editor. You write the chapter wherever you prefer, and record here who was in the scene, what changed hands, and which world rule that respects.

anywhere.title: Phone, web, and desktop
anywhere.body: The same client on Android, iOS, the browser, and Windows, macOS, and Linux. At home, Keres Server on a PC syncs the phone without Docker or PostgreSQL.

product.title: One place for the whole story
product.lead: Open a story and the side menu lists every kind of element. Lists with search, filters, and favorites; records with relationships; graphs when space or choices ask for a map.

universe.title: The narrative universe
universe.lead: Everything a story needs to keep, linked together.

characters.title: Characters
characters.body: Who takes part, what describes them, and how they stay coherent across the work.

relations.title: Relationships
relations.body: Bonds between people — family, rivalry, mentorship — and a graph of the cast.

modes.title: Modes
modes.body: The forms a character takes: transformations, disguises, lasting states.

stats.title: Stats
stats.body: Axes you define and a radar chart to compare the cast, with letter or number notation.

chapters.title: Chapters
chapters.body: Group scenes in reading order or in the chronology you choose.

scenes.title: Scenes
scenes.body: Each event: where it happens, who is there, and what takes place.

timing.title: Scene timing
timing.body: How long each event lasts and the gap until the next one.

locations.title: Locations
locations.body: The spaces of the story, with containment and path relationships.

locationMap.title: Location map
locationMap.body: A graph of places inside places and the links between them.

items.title: Items
items.body: Important objects, their initial state, and who holds them.

itemJourneys.title: Item journeys
itemJourneys.body: Scene by scene, when an object changes state or owner.

worldRules.title: World rules
worldRules.body: Limits and facts the universe must respect to stay coherent.

notes.title: Notes
notes.body: Free writing, loose or anchored to any story element.

tags.title: Tags
tags.body: Colored labels, applicable to any kind of element.

gallery.title: Gallery
gallery.body: Images, audio, and video, reusable across records.

favorites.title: Favorites
favorites.body: Highlight what matters now and filter lists by it.

branching.title: Branching stories
branching.lead: For CYOA, games, and any narrative with more than one path.

type.title: Linear or branching
type.body: A linear story follows scene order. A branching one links scenes through choices.

choices.title: Choices
choices.body: The decision text, the source scene, and the destination.

storyMap.title: Story map
storyMap.body: A navigable diagram of scenes and transitions, so the graph is visible at once.

conditions.title: Conditions
conditions.body: A choice only appears if the reader visited a scene, holds an item, or flipped a flag.

effects.title: Effects
effects.body: Give or take an item, turn a flag on or off, when passing through a scene or a decision.

storyState.title: Reader state
storyState.body: What the reader carries — visits, inventory, flags — analyzed together with the map.

craft.title: Craft tools
craft.lead: Find, extend, and review the plan without leaving the app.

customAttributes.title: Custom attributes
customAttributes.body: Your own fields on characters, locations, items, scenes, chapters, notes, and rules: text, number, date, boolean, or suggestion.

suggestions.title: Suggestions
suggestions.body: Per-story lists for races, genders, relationship types, and whatever else repeats.

search.title: Search
search.body: Global search across every field, including custom attributes, and advanced search on each list.

analysis.title: Story analysis
analysis.body: Orphan scenes, broken choices, and other structural issues an author rarely spots alone.

dashboard.title: Story dashboard
dashboard.body: A snapshot of what is already planned and shortcuts to what still needs review.

comments.title: Comments
comments.body: Threads anchored to a field or an element, also gathered in one list.

seeAlso.title: See also
seeAlso.body: A free, reciprocal link between two elements, without replacing tags or notes.

storyDevices.title: Literary devices
storyDevices.body: A reference list of narrative techniques — foreshadowing, hooks, ticking clocks — kept apart from your story.

help.title: Built-in help
help.body: A Portuguese and English catalog, with local search and a help icon on every screen.

exampleStories.title: Example stories
exampleStories.body: Install a ready-made copy to explore Keres without touching your own work.

together.title: Sync, collaborate, publish
together.lead: The server is optional. When it exists, it is the bridge between devices and between people.

offlineSync.title: Synchronization
offlineSync.body: Work offline. When you connect, the engine replicates creates, edits, and deletes with version checks.

servers.title: Servers
servers.body: Register a Keres Server URL or a Docker API and bind stories to it.

friends.title: Friends
friends.body: Friend requests on the same server, the first step to inviting someone.

collaborators.title: Collaborators
collaborators.body: Invite friends to read or edit a synced story, with permissions on the story itself.

conflicts.title: Conflicts
conflicts.body: If two edits start from the same version, Keres surfaces the conflict instead of silently dropping one.

activityLog.title: Operation log
activityLog.body: An auditable history of what was created, changed, or deleted during sync.

publish.title: Publish
publish.body: Some servers run a showcase: a frozen copy of the Keres database, for anyone to download and import.

importExport.title: Import and export
importExport.body: A story package on the device, for backup, handing off, or publishing.

platforms.title: Where Keres runs
platforms.lead: One client, several ways to reach it. A server, when you want one.

android.title: Android
android.body: APK and AAB on each release. The same app as on iOS, with local SQLite.

ios.title: iOS
ios.body: Native Expo client. Plan on the phone and sync with the PC at home.

web.title: Web
web.body: The client also runs in the browser. That is the build the desktop app wraps.

windows.title: Windows
windows.body: Installer and portable executable, produced with every version.

macos.title: macOS
macos.body: DMG for Apple Silicon and Intel, unsigned until a certificate exists.

linux.title: Linux
linux.body: AppImage and Flatpak on the same releases as everything else.

keresServer.title: Keres Server
keresServer.body: The API on SQLite, with a Portuguese and English wizard. No Docker, no Postgres: unzip and run.

docker.title: Docker
docker.body: An image on GHCR with PostgreSQL, the /admin panel, and media storage. For whoever runs a real server.

download.title: Download and start
download.lead: Official builds ship on GitHub Releases, together with Keres Server and the Docker image.

releases.title: Client
releases.body: Desktop for Windows, macOS, and Linux, plus Android. Open the latest release and pick the file for your system.

server.title: Keres Server
server.body: Zips for Windows x64, Linux x64, and macOS Apple Silicon. On first run the wizard asks for the database, media, and port.

docker.title: Docker image
docker.body: ghcr.io/caiofviana/keres — prefer an immutable tag in production. The repo ships a deploy Compose file.

source.title: Source code
source.body: An open monorepo: client, API, admin panel, desktop, and this landing page. Bun, TypeScript, tests in CI.

stack.title: How it is built
stack.lead: The same pieces described in the repository documentation.
stack.client: React Native + Expo, local SQLite, Zustand stores, and a custom sync engine.
stack.desktop: Electron around the client's web build, with SQLite in OPFS.
stack.api: Bun, Elysia, Drizzle. PostgreSQL in Docker; SQLite in the home Keres Server.
stack.admin: A React panel served by the API at /admin, for accounts, plans, and registration.
stack.shared: Entities, Zod contracts, and palettes shared across the apps.

editor.q: Does Keres replace my text editor?
editor.a: No. It organizes the narrative universe. The manuscript, script, or campaign stays where you already write.

offline.a: Not to plan. The client keeps everything on the device. A network is only needed to sync, collaborate, or publish on a server.

server.a: No. A story can live only on the device. A server comes in when you want the same universe on the phone and the PC, or when you want to collaborate.

languages.q: Which languages is the app in?
languages.a: Portuguese and English, in the client, the help, Keres Server, and this page.

collaborate.q: Can more than one person write it?
collaborate.a: With a server: invite friends, choose whether they read or edit, and comment on records. Without a server, you can hand off an import/export package.

cost.a: Keres is open software. You download the client and, if you want, run your own server. An operator of a public server may apply account limits — that is their decision, not the application's.

showcase.a: No. This is the project landing page. The showcase of published stories is a separate site, served by a Keres Server someone chose to run.

footer.tagline: A writing companion for planning stories.
